To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• the inference algorithm implemented as a stored procedure is more efficient than the inference performed on preloaded knowledge base, • the inference algorithm as a stored procedure can be used as a tool for building the rule-based expert systems, and • the inference algorithm can be implemented using the standard programming tools and the SQL language.

(a) the use of stored procedures is effective for inference on small rule bases (less than 200 rules), and (b) the use of the stored procedure is not effective for inference on large rule bases (more than 500 rules).
using stored procedure to perform inference on a knowledge base stored in a relational database is a viable solution for the expert system shell, which can be used in the real-world systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new approaches to building distributed rule-based expert systems and with the evaluation of these approaches.
the development of new inference algorithms for distributed knowledge-based applications.
the following issues: 1) the development of the inference algorithm as the stored procedure, 2) the evaluation of this approach, 3) the comparison with other inference algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is effective and the results obtained by this way can be considered as the basis for further research.
the utilization of stored procedures for inference is effective, when the inference algorithm is implemented in a database programming language.
the use of stored procedures for inference is an effective solution, especially for large and complex knowledge bases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of database stored procedures for performing inference is an effective way of inference for large rule bases and is suitable for mobile and embedded systems.
the inference performed as the stored procedure is faster for large knowledge bases, but the difference between the approaches is not so big.
the inference performed on the stored procedures can be considered as a promising alternative for inference on the preloaded rule bases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of database procedures is not a panacea for the problem of the inference in the distributed expert system.
the inference on stored procedures is more effective than inference on preloaded knowledge bases, especially for large knowledge bases.
it is possible to use a stored procedure for the inference and that this approach is effective for large knowledge bases.
